gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Birdfy cameras will not join a WPA3-only Wi-Fi network (the router must be set to WPA2 or WPA/WPA2 mixed). The results also do not give the full band split behind that: most Birdfy feeders, including the Feeder 2 Pro, Metal S and older Feeder units, are 2.4 GHz only, while the 2026 Feeder Metal 2 4K and the current Birdbuddy Home also do 5 GHz.
standout_why: I read feederfield.com (rank 1) and birdfeederlab.com (rank 3). WebFetch was blocked on the two cited pages, wired.com and goodhousekeeping.com, so I could not check them. Feederfield already lists Wi-Fi bands for each model: Birdbuddy Pro Solar 2.4 GHz plus Bluetooth for setup, Birdbuddy Home 2.4 and 5 GHz, and Birdfy Feeder 2, 2 Pro and 2 Duo 2.4 GHz only. Birdfeederlab only says to check for a strong 2.4 GHz signal. Neither page mentions the WPA3-only exclusion. Neither names the Birdfy Feeder Metal 2 4K as dual-band, or says the 2K Birdfy Feeder comes in an older 2.4 GHz-only version and a newer 2.4/5 GHz version. Neither gives Bird Buddy's own warnings: no USB-A-to-USB-C charging cable, and no hidden network. Neither says which Bird Buddy add-ons fit which feeder, or gives the maker's low-temperature limits (Birdfy 14°F, Birdbuddy Home −5°F).
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. ChatGPT's 'best overall', the Birdbuddy Pro Solar ($199.99 at Target), is the previous generation and 2.4 GHz only. Bird Buddy's own shop sells the Birdbuddy Home for $199 (was $219), with solar panels built into the roof, dual-band 2.4/5 GHz Wi-Fi and a lower −5°F operating limit. Bird Buddy's Perch Extender ($39) and Wall Mount fit the Home as well as the Pro. For a Birdfy, a shopper on a WPA3-only or 5 GHz-only mesh router must either change the router's security setting or buy the Feeder Metal 2 4K ($199.99 at birdfy.com), the dual-band Birdfy we list. The Feeder 2 Pro ($219.99) is 2.4 GHz only.

findings.label: Wi-Fi security exclusion
findings.value: Birdfy cameras do not support WPA3-only encryption. The router must be set to WPA2 or WPA/WPA2 Mixed.
findings.note: Section 3.2 of 'My device fails to connect to Wi-Fi after scanning the QR code', quoted: "Birdfy cameras do not support WPA3-only encryption." Section 3.5 says that if pairing fails, test with a 2.4 GHz phone hotspot and then pair to a guest network on the router (Eero given as the example).

findings.value: Most Birdfy products: 2.4 GHz only. From 2026 some newer models, such as the Birdfy Feeder Metal 2 4K, support both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz.
